events.title: Franklin Pierce Is Born
events.description: Franklin Pierce, who became the 14th President of the United States, was born in Hillsborough, New Hampshire. The son of a Revolutionary War veteran, he rose through state politics and the U.S. Congress before winning the presidency in 1852.
events.significance: Pierce's presidency (1853–1857) was marked by the Kansas-Nebraska Act, which deepened the national divide over slavery in the years before the Civil War.

events.title: The First Issue of LIFE Magazine Is Published
events.description: Henry Luce's new picture-driven weekly magazine hit newsstands with a cover photograph of the Fort Peck Dam in Montana. Its first issue also featured photographs by Alfred Eisenstaedt.
events.significance: LIFE helped establish photojournalism as a mass medium and shaped how generations of Americans saw world events.

events.title: Doctor Who Debuts on British Television
events.description: The BBC broadcast the first episode of a new science-fiction series, 'An Unearthly Child', introducing a mysterious time-traveling Doctor and the TARDIS.
events.significance: It became the longest-running science-fiction television series in the world, and it has been reinvented many times with new actors in the lead role.

events.title: Ellen Johnson Sirleaf Is Declared Winner of Liberia's Presidential Election
events.description: Liberia's election commission declared Ellen Johnson Sirleaf the winner of the country's presidential runoff, following the end of the nation's long civil wars.
events.significance: She became the first woman elected head of state in an African country and later shared the 2011 Nobel Peace Prize.

events.title: The Maguindanao Massacre
events.description: In the southern Philippines, gunmen killed 57 people, including 34 journalists, who were traveling in a convoy to file election paperwork for a local politician, Esmael Mangudadatu.
events.significance: It is considered the deadliest single attack on journalists in recorded history and drew global attention to press freedom and political violence.
